newsitem.title: UK: Consumer foods lift Dairy Crest H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Consumer foods lift Dairy Crest H1 results.

text.p: British milk and cheese group Dairy Crest Group Plc said on Tuesday its pretax profits rose in the first half, boosted by the strong performance of its consumer foods segment.

The farmer-controlled company, reporting earnings for the first time since its flotation in August, said its first-half pretax profits grew to 16.5 million pounds ($27.02 million) on a pro forma basis compared to 15.4 million in the year-ago period.
Total turnover advanced to 381.6 million pounds from 365.0 million in the prior period, which included 9.5 million pounds from discontinued operations.
The company also set an interim dividend of 3.26p per share.
"We are particularly pleased with the encouraging growth in the consumer foods segment and the resilience of our food services business," the company said in a statement.
It added that its consumer foods segment should continue to make progress, while market conditions for its food services business were likely to be similar to those in the first half.
Dairy Crest's shares slid five pence to 198.5 at 1050 GMT.
Sales for the company's consumer foods businesses rose 22 percent to 218.3 million pounds in the first half, while operating profit jumped 42 percent to 12.9 million pounds.
However, the food services business posted declines, with turnover down eight percent at 163.3 million pounds and operating profit falling 1.1 million pounds to 6.4 million.

"As anticipated, the results of this segment have reflected the reversal of last year's strong market pricing for commodity ingredients products," Dairy Crest said, adding that the continued decline in doorstep milk operations also hurt results.
Dairy Crest, the former manufacturing arm of the defunct Milk Marketing Board, priced its flotation in August at 155 pence per share, valuing the firm at about 171 million pounds.
The company said two non-executive directors, BUPA chief executive Peter Jacobs and Hays Plc chairman Ronnie Frost, would step down at the end of the year after having helped with its flotation.
Dairy Crest planned to replace them with a new commercial non-executive director. ($1=.6107 Pound)
